shared_elements: low-relief carving on weathered porous stone
row of repeated arch-like/loop or bracket motifs across the top edge
horizontal dividing band of repeated pattern (hatching / stacked bars)
animal or creature heads in profile
quadruped-like figures with limbs shown in profile
small circles or discs set among the figures
isolated small bar-like or handled elements
justification: The most specific correspondence is structural: both surfaces open at the top with a row of repeated arch/loop-like motifs, are then cut by a horizontal band of repetitive linear pattern, and carry profile animal or creature figures with scattered discs in the field below. The biggest difference is density and handling — A is a crowded, deeply modelled and heavily overlapping composition of rounded, quasi-glyphic heads filling every space, while B is sparse, flat and outline-driven, with a few widely spaced figures on a smooth ground, and the two supports differ in shape (rectangular slab versus tall shouldered pillar).
